mechanism_narrative: Persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.5%) signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses equity discount rates, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% (t-test p>0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% over three months signals economic weakness that triggers immediate equity sell-offs, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when UNRATE > 5.0% (t-test p>0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in UNRATE indicates monetary policy ineffectiveness during economic stress, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of FEDFUNDS decline and UNRATE rise does not produce negative 20-day returns in 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDP growth >2% and unemployment <4.5%), rising consumer credit (RSAFS) signals overoptimism that precedes equity corrections, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods meeting the late-cycle condition (GDPC1>2% and UNRATE<4.5%) despite rising RSAFS.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production (INDPRO) falling below 105.0 for two consecutive months signals manufacturing contraction that triggers equity market declines, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when INDPRO < 105.0 (t-test p>0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) below 1,100,000 units for two consecutive months signals weak consumer demand that precedes equity market corrections, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in 60% or more of periods when HOUST < 1100.0 (t-test p>0.05 vs. baseline).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE indicates labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS decline and UNRATE rise does not produce negative 60-day returns in 60% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03).

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth (GDPC1 above 2.0% annualized) signals robust economic expansion that supports equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in 60% or more of periods when GDPC1 > 2.0% (t-test p>0.05 vs. baseline).
